sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Gandhian Strategy**: Based on **Satyagraha** (truth-force) and **Ahimsa** (non-violence), shifting the movement from urban centers to the rural masses.
• **Ideological Pluralism**: The phase witnessed the rise of **Socialists** (J.P. Narayan, Acharya Narendra Dev), **Revolutionaries** (Bhagat Singh, Azad), and **Constitutionalists** (Swarajists like C.R. Das, Motilal Nehru).
• **Mass Mobilization**: Transition from 'Petition-Prayer-Protest' to 'Non-Cooperation-Civil Disobedience-Quit India' as the primary **mechanisms of resistance**.
• **Key Metric**: The ability of leaders to bridge the gap between the **Congress High Command** and the **grassroots peasantry/labor unions**.

The policy of entering the Legislative Councils to wreck the British administration from within, adopted after the failure of the Non-Cooperation Movement.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22)**: First pan-India mass movement.
• **Civil Disobedience (1930-34)**: Use of symbolic acts (Salt Satyagraha) to challenge colonial legitimacy.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Communalism, caste divisions, and ideological splits within the INC.
• **Solutions**: Formation of the Congress Socialist Party and the integration of the Princely States.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'G-S-S-R' (Gandhian, Swarajist, Socialist, Revolutionary).
• **Decoded Meaning**: G (Gandhian/Constructive), S (Swarajist/Legislative), S (Socialist/Labor-Peasant), R (Revolutionary/Armed).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Pro-changers' (Swarajists) with the 'No-changers' (Gandhian loyalists). Remember: Pro-changers wanted to enter councils; No-changers wanted to continue the Constructive Program.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Multi-vocal movement' to describe the Third Phase, highlighting how diverse ideologies co-existed under the umbrella of the Indian National Congress.

keyTakeaways: The Third Phase was defined by the shift from elite constitutionalism to mass-based civil disobedience.
Ideological diversity (Socialists vs. Conservatives) was a strength, not just a weakness, of the INC.
Gandhiji acted as the 'Great Unifier' who balanced radical and moderate factions.
